content.user_title: Analyze Scheduled Jobs and Agent Run History
content.value_statement: Exported job histories can make recurring failures and slow runs difficult to assess. CronPulse organizes supplied records into evidence-backed incident summaries and reliability metrics.
actual_capabilities: Review exported JSON arrays or JSONL run-history files.
Normalize common job names, statuses, timestamps, durations, exit codes, and error fields.
Group runs by job or task to identify failures, duration outliers, repeated errors, and missing or invalid fields.
Calculate counts and success rates from supplied records, stating the denominator and excluded records.
Summarize actionable incidents with timestamps and source evidence.
Recommend manual next checks while separating confirmed failures from suspected causes.
limitations: Requires supplied exports; it does not connect to cron, GitHub Actions, n8n, or agent platforms.
Cannot detect runs missing from the supplied export.
Cannot send alerts, retry jobs, restart tasks, or provide live monitoring.
Cannot establish root cause from a status label alone.

use_cases.title: Review Scheduled Job Reliability
use_cases.description: Analyze exported job runs to identify failures, slow executions, and repeated errors before selecting manual follow-up checks.

use_cases.title: Investigate Agent Run Failures
use_cases.description: Group exported AI-agent runs by task and summarize confirmed failures with timestamps and error evidence.

use_cases.title: Prepare Workflow Incident Summaries
use_cases.description: Turn exported automation histories into concise reliability reviews that state success-rate denominators and data-quality limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted run-history export. Summarize failures and repeated errors using only the supplied records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a JSON array or JSONL export.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Reliability by Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Group this export by job or task. Report run counts, success rates, denominators, excluded records, and missing or invalid fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate reliability reporting across multiple jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Incident Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify actionable failures, non-zero exit codes, unusually long durations, and repeated errors in this export. Include timestamps and source evidence for each incident.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed incident triage from supplied history.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence-Based Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Normalize this mixed-field export and group runs by task. State metric denominators and exclusions. Separate confirmed failures from suspected causes and recommend manual checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of inconsistent run-history records.

output_examples.input: Illustrative export: ten valid backup runs, eight successful and two failed with the same timeout message.
output: Backup success rate: 80%, based on eight successful runs out of ten supplied runs; no records excluded.
Two failures share a timeout message. The repeated error is confirmed, but the underlying cause is not established.
Manual next check: inspect the supplied failure timestamps and corresponding backup logs.

output_examples.input: Illustrative export: four successful report runs lasting 30, 32, 31, and 300 seconds.
output: Report success rate: 100%, based on four successful runs out of four supplied runs; no records excluded.
The 300-second run is unusually long compared with the other three supplied runs.
The duration difference does not establish a cause. Manually compare logs and workload details for the slow run.

best_practices: Provide redacted exports that retain job names, timestamps, statuses, durations, exit codes, and relevant error messages.
Check reported denominators and exclusions before comparing success rates.
Use incident evidence to guide manual checks, and keep suspected causes separate from confirmed failures.
anti_patterns: Providing credentials or live access tokens instead of a redacted export.
Treating an incomplete export as proof that no other runs occurred.
Assuming a failure status proves root cause or triggers automatic recovery.

faq.question: What input formats does CronPulse review?
faq.answer: It reviews exported JSON arrays or JSONL run-history files, including redacted samples.

faq.question: Does it connect to live scheduling platforms?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes supplied exports and does not connect to cron, GitHub Actions, n8n, or agent platforms.

faq.question: Which fields can it normalize?
faq.answer: Common fields include job or task names, statuses, timestamps, durations, exit codes, and error messages.

faq.question: How are success rates calculated?
faq.answer: Calculations use supplied records only. The review states the denominator and identifies excluded records.

faq.question: Can it alert me or retry failed jobs?
faq.answer: No. It recommends manual next checks but cannot send alerts, retry jobs, or restart tasks.

faq.question: Can it determine why a job failed?
faq.answer: It separates confirmed failures from suspected causes. A status label alone does not establish root cause.
